_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `CadMutation` is a semio-NATIVE vocabulary carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no oracle is registered and the decision below records what stands in for one.

oracles.rationale:
A second implementation of the `s.cad.cad` document and all twenty typed mutations, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-cad-1/🐍️component.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️component.json` (the members and which of them are optional), rules 1, 2 and 7 of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md`, and the twenty committed `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintets — which are the only statement of four things: that a `create-<slot>-model` verb carries its child id EXPLICITLY rather than content-addressing it; that it REHANDLES an occupied slot instead of refusing; that a `delete-<slot>-model` REMOVES the member from the document rather than nulling it; and that `replace-reference-media` rewrites five members of one reference and leaves its placement and flags alone. The reference also implements the child-target wire spelling `"<artifactId>!<artifactKind>@<standard>/<subset>"` in both directions, because the mutation payloads carry it as one string while the snapshot carries it expanded — a reader that never split it could not reproduce a single `create-` vector. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. This registration SUPERSEDES the `cad-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision, whose argument — that the child-slot lifecycle "IS this subset's specification, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute", and that a general-purpose CAD or JSON-patch crate would be a worse reference than none — was refuted in this same wave by `mutate-gismap-1`, which took a Python second implementation over this same carrier. The old decision was right that a third-party CAD library is the wrong reference and wrong that the only alternative is no reference; a second implementation written from this subset's own schemas is neither. ALL TWENTY KINDS ARE ADJUDICATED AND NONE IS REFUSED: every child id in this vocabulary is supplied by the caller, so unlike `s.block.3d`'s `catalog` or `s.architect.program`'s `knowledge`/`benchmarks`, nothing here depends on a content-addressing function no specification states. ONE CEILING ON WHAT THIS COMPARISON ESTABLISHES: the SUBJECT half does not run this subset's codec — `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-cad-1/🦀️component.rs` links no plugin crate and replays the committed vectors — so today it establishes that an independent implementation of the specification computes the committed after-snapshots, not yet our codec against a second producer. A `cad_mutation_report_json` bridge beside the mutation enum closes it; it is not added here for two reasons, and neither is that the verb is hard: it is PRODUCTION code in a crate this test-side pass deliberately does not touch, and it could not be verified end to end today anyway. `parity` was not measured for any case in this pass: the single-case probe `parity exhaustive --owner 🗒️note --case mutate-note-1` was killed at the runner's OWN 900 s per-case budget while still COMPILING the generated subject host — the runner's message names the cause, shared cargo target-dir lock contention from a concurrent session — and then threw `spawnSync cargo ETIMEDOUT` out of `runProbe` with no summary line at all. `📓️w14-final-audit.md` §5.3 measured the underlying blocker one day earlier (`unresolved import component::component_persistent_local` in `semio-framework-plugin`, which sits in every generated host's dependency graph); this pass did NOT re-verify whether that is still the state, and says so rather than repeating it as fact. This subset's own plugin crate compiles clean at `cargo check --lib`. This case also reads no real-world artifact: all 100 of its fixtures are handcrafted specification vectors. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `cad-1-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 20-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.
